questions.q: When market yields rise, the price of an existing bond with a fixed coupon rises.
questions.why: Price and yield move in opposite directions: the fixed coupon becomes less attractive, so the price falls.

questions.q: Why does the yield curve usually slope upwards?
options: Lenders want more for tying money up longer and taking more rate and inflation risk
questions.why: Longer loans carry more uncertainty, so investors usually demand higher yields.

questions.q: What happened in UK bond markets after the September 2022 mini-budget?
options: Gilt yields jumped, pension LDI strategies were forced to sell, and the Bank of England bought long gilts
questions.why: Falling prices forced leveraged pension strategies to sell, deepening the fall until the Bank stepped in.

questions.q: A bond pays £5 a year and returns £100 in exactly one year. The market yield is {y}%. What's its price today? (£, 2 dp)
Explain why an existing bond's price falls when interest rates rise.

ideas.label: Its coupon is fixed, so new bonds now pay more
Its price falls until its yield matches the market (less attractive)

questions.model: Its coupon was fixed when it was issued. When rates rise, new bonds pay more, so nobody will pay full price for the old one. Its price falls until its yield is competitive with the market.
questions.why: A fixed payment is worth less when better ones are on offer.

tests.answer: Its coupon is fixed and new bonds pay more, so its price falls until its yield matches the market.

questions.q: Explain why a UK government bond can lose value even though the government is very unlikely to default.

ideas.label: If yields rise, its price falls (interest rate risk), especially long bonds
Inflation can shrink the real value of fixed payments

questions.model: If market yields rise, the price of an existing gilt falls, a lot for long bonds, so anyone selling before maturity can lose money. And inflation can shrink what its fixed payments are worth in real terms.
questions.why: No default risk isn't the same as no risk.

tests.answer: If yields rise its price falls, especially for long bonds, and inflation reduces the real value of the payments.
Its price falls when interest rates rise.
Because the government might go bankrupt tomorrow.
